findings.evidence: The protected route gate compares X-API-Key against a hard-coded, publicly committed placeholder. Exact credential value is redacted.
findings.verification_procedure: Read the auth constant and the authed() branch; physical missing/wrong/correct-key requests were not sent.
findings.impact: A device flashed without replacing the placeholder accepts known credentials for reachable mutating routes, including feed and clear/configuration requests.
findings.exploitability: Requires network reachability to the CAM and that the committed placeholder remains configured.
findings.recommended_fix: Provision a unique per-device credential outside source control; rotate deployed credentials; use network segmentation and rate limits; test the exact authorization matrix on an isolated device.
findings.retest_result: Not retested on hardware; firmware changes require authorization.

findings.evidence: CAM POST /api/abort sends ABORT and returns 202; WROOM command parser has no ABORT branch. No gate-close abort outcome is emitted.
findings.verification_procedure: Static producer-to-parser trace; no physical abort test was attempted.
findings.impact: User may believe an active dispense can be stopped when the WROOM will ignore the command.
findings.exploitability: Any accepted abort request while a dispense is active; reachable to a client with the device API key.
findings.recommended_fix: Implement immediate gate close and an abort state/result on WROOM; return correlated ACK/NAK and publish the final outcome.
findings.retest_result: Not retested; actuator tests need an explicitly safe hardware procedure.

findings.evidence: Dispense timeout enters SETTLE; if net weight is below target, TOPUP opens the gate for 250 ms and returns to SETTLE. There is no top-up count limit or stale-scale check.
findings.verification_procedure: State-transition trace from ST_DISPENSE timeout through ST_SETTLE and ST_TOPUP; not physically exercised.
findings.impact: With no weight increase or stale load-cell values, successive top-ups can repeatedly reopen the gate and exceed the requested portion.
findings.exploitability: Requires a load-cell fault or persistent under-reading during dispensing.
findings.recommended_fix: Bound top-up count and total actuation time, verify sensor readiness/freshness, and latch a fault with the gate closed on timeout.
findings.retest_result: Not retested; requires firmware change and isolated bench test.

findings.evidence: CAM sends two uncorrelated feed commands, FEED_NOW and FEED. WROOM recognizes only FEED_NOW, has no request ID/deduplication, and CAM returns constant ID 1 before a WROOM response.
findings.verification_procedure: Static command producer/consumer scan in static_contract_results.json; hardware ACK/retry tests unavailable.
findings.impact: A retry or delayed duplicate cannot be safely distinguished from a new dispense, and the HTTP accepted response does not establish that WROOM accepted the job.
findings.exploitability: Network delay, lost responses, repeated requests, or clients retrying a timed-out request.
findings.recommended_fix: Use one versioned framed command with unique request ID, bounded dedupe state, explicit ACK/NAK, and correlated final completion event.
findings.retest_result: Static scan confirms mismatch remains; no firmware change applied.

findings.evidence: WROOM never emits TELEM JSON; CAM status starts with fixed synthetic telemetry. WROOM emits only LOG amount; CAM fabricates source, target, weights, result=OK and timestamp. CAM GET /api/log returns an unchanged [] buffer.
findings.verification_procedure: Source trace from WROOM output to CAM parser and frontend mapping; static scanner reports no WROOM TELEM producer.
findings.impact: UI can display stale/synthetic state or a fabricated successful feed record, confusing safety decisions and audit history.
findings.exploitability: Normal hardware operation with the checked-in WROOM sketch.
findings.recommended_fix: Define validated telemetry and full log frames, preserve device timestamps/results/request IDs, and expose unknown data as unavailable rather than defaults.
findings.retest_result: Not retested with hardware. Web command messages were changed to avoid claiming confirmation for selected 202 operations.

findings.evidence: CAM sends CLEAR, SCHED, TARE, CAL, CFG; WROOM has no corresponding handlers. WROOM clockService schedule implementation is an explicit TODO.
findings.verification_procedure: Static source contract scan; no UART hardware test.
findings.impact: Dashboard actions return 202 but do not change device fault, schedule, tare, calibration, or configuration state.
findings.exploitability: Normal use of those dashboard actions.
findings.recommended_fix: Implement validated handlers and correlated completion outcomes or disable the matching frontend controls until supported.
findings.retest_result: Frontend messages now describe acceptance, not completion; protocol defects remain.

findings.evidence: Async body callbacks ignore index/total and JSON deserialization errors; raw schedule/config chunks are converted as NUL-terminated strings without an explicit bounded accumulator. No schema/content-type/maximum-size validation is present.
findings.verification_procedure: Static review; malformed/chunked requests were not sent to a device.
findings.impact: Malformed requests may fall back to defaults or be forwarded; chunked or oversized content may be truncated or consume excessive memory. The pointer-to-string use is a potential out-of-bounds read depending on callback buffer termination semantics.
findings.exploitability: Reachable CAM endpoint plus accepted key for mutating calls; unauthenticated fields are not applicable.
findings.recommended_fix: Bound body size, accumulate by index/total, parse once, check parse errors and content type, reject unknown fields/types/ranges, and safely copy chunks.

findings.evidence: WROOM converts FEED_NOW suffix with toInt and does not enforce a local portion range. PRECHECK does not reject low/unknown hopper state or invalid/stale scale values. Low-food reporting is separate from feed authorization.
findings.verification_procedure: Static control-flow trace; malformed UART values and sensor failure were not injected on hardware.
findings.impact: A faulty or compromised upstream sender can request unsafe portions; sensor faults may not fail closed.
findings.exploitability: UART sender can inject a command or CAM validation is bypassed/changed.
findings.recommended_fix: Enforce independent WROOM portion limits, validate numeric syntax, require fresh sensor readings, detect missing echo/load-cell readiness, and fail closed.

findings.evidence: Read routes, snapshot and SSE have no auth check; CORS allows any origin.
findings.verification_procedure: Static route-auth map; actual unauthenticated requests not sent.
findings.impact: Reachable clients can inspect feeder state, history, schedules, camera images and pet events.
findings.exploitability: Network reachability to device; wildcard CORS makes cross-origin browser reads possible where network policy allows.
findings.recommended_fix: Define the intended LAN trust boundary; isolate device network; gate data access through an authenticated same-origin proxy or another EventSource-compatible authorization design.

findings.evidence: WROOM schedule execution is TODO, lastFedToken is unused, and CAM stores schedule only in RAM. CAM can echo a new array without WROOM persistence.
findings.verification_procedure: Static source trace; power-cycle/schedule tests unavailable.
findings.impact: Schedules and once-per-day duplicate protection described in UI/docs are not implemented in this firmware pair.
findings.exploitability: Normal scheduled operation or CAM restart.
findings.recommended_fix: Implement validated schedule storage/execution and durable per-slot run tokens with RTC validity and reboot tests.

findings.evidence: Text commands use delimiters only; there is no checksum/CRC, explicit max frame length, dedupe ID, or bounded parser recovery. Arduino String and readStringUntil are used; WROOM also has blocking delays in state handling.
findings.verification_procedure: Static parser inspection; no UART frame harness was available.
findings.impact: Corrupted/truncated/oversized frames may be ignored unpredictably or consume memory/time; no integrity/authenticity guarantee exists.
findings.exploitability: Physical UART access, electrical noise, or a compromised CAM.
findings.recommended_fix: Use bounded versioned frames, CRC for accidental corruption, strict length/syntax validation, resynchronization and ACK/NAK. CRC does not authenticate a sender; secure the physical/network trust boundary separately.

findings.evidence: The code starts an asynchronous response using framebuffer memory and returns the framebuffer immediately afterward. The exact installed AsyncWebServer copy/ownership behavior is unknown.
findings.verification_procedure: Source inspection only; no camera frame transfer or library version available.
findings.impact: If the response retains the pointer, the frame could be reused before the HTTP send completes.
findings.exploitability: Concurrent camera capture/HTTP traffic and library response semantics.
findings.recommended_fix: Confirm library ownership; retain the framebuffer until completion or copy bytes into response-owned storage.
findings.retest_result: Blocked on firmware dependencies and hardware.

findings.evidence: No test/lint scripts, CI workflow, firmware build manifest, or checked-in firmware unit tests were found.
findings.verification_procedure: Read package scripts and tracked file inventory.
findings.impact: Contract regressions can merge without automated detection.
findings.exploitability: Process weakness, not a direct vulnerability.
findings.recommended_fix: Add static contract tests, frontend tests, reproducible firmware builds, and CI gates once protocol contracts are explicit.
findings.retest_result: Static audit and proxy smoke scripts were added under audit; no CI workflow added.

findings.evidence: The report calls the integration production-grade and says the CAM file duplicates WROOM; current sketch hashes show CAM copies match each other and WROOM copies match each other. Report also describes telemetry/schedule behavior absent from WROOM source.
findings.verification_procedure: Compared report assertions to both sketch copies and source handlers.
findings.impact: Operators may flash the wrong file or assume nonexistent features are verified.
findings.recommended_fix: Replace the report with source-traceable contracts and hardware evidence; retain explicit unverified status until actual tests.
findings.retest_result: Report is outside writable workspace and was left untouched.

findings.evidence: CAM turns WROOM IR PET_DETECTED into a fixed pet verdict and confidence. No inference model or temporal voting implementation exists in the CAM sketch.
findings.verification_procedure: Source search and event trace; no image classification run.
findings.impact: UI may imply a TinyML classification that did not occur.
findings.recommended_fix: Label as IR presence until a model and actual inference path are implemented and tested.
